product: MM-FUR-001 Corner cabinet with glass display top (Eckkommode)

scope.intended_use: Free-standing corner cabinet, 1000 mm high, filling a right-angled room niche whose two walls are nominally 1 m wide. Pentagonal footprint with a single flat 45 deg diagonal front, 1081.9 mm wide, carrying four identical 539 x 439 mm doors in a 2x2 grid, one fixed mid shelf, six height-adjustable feet, and a flat timber top plate at 1000 mm with a loose 6 mm ESG glass plate laid directly on it so postcards can be displayed between wood and glass. Manufactured from 18 mm white-painted real-wood panels cut by a DIY-store panel service and assembled with purchased furniture hardware. Revision 0.2.0 shortened the side returns from 340 to 200 mm so the front projects 131 mm rather than 230 mm past the line joining the two wall ends; the legs stay at 965 mm, so the niche is still filled, and the doors widened from 440 to 539 mm as the geometric consequence.
scope.user_context: Private indoor dry living space, single owner-built unit, adult users, child access UNKNOWN. Assembly happens in place because the assembled mass is about 80 kg.
variants: Material variant A (recommended): 18 mm birch plywood (Multiplex Birke) throughout
Material variant B: 18 mm glued solid spruce or pine panel (Leimholz), cut to size
Optional: 22 mm top plate instead of 18 mm (changes vertical panel height, parameter-driven)

Rejected at owner decision 2026-09-05: shortening the legs together with the side returns (850 mm legs would project only 67 mm and keep 440 mm doors, at the cost of 140 mm of free wall at each end and 28 % of the display top)
out_of_scope: Wall anchoring as a structural load path
Electrical, lighting, locks, drawers, soft-close upgrade
Any commercial release of the design or the built object
FDM printing: no printed part exists in this product

entities.name: Carcass panel set, 18 mm, custom-cut timber (custom-fabricated part; the schema enum has no timber category)
Four door panels 539 x 439 x 18 mm, custom-cut timber
Pentagonal top display plate, custom-cut timber
Pentagonal 6 mm ESG glass plate, made to measure, polished edges
8 x 35 mm cup hinge, half-overlay (Mittelanschlag), with cross mounting plates
4 x bow handle, 128 mm hole spacing
6 x height-adjustable furniture foot, 100 mm, M8, screw-on plate
Screws, angle brackets, 20 x 20 mm battens, wood glue, door buffers
Primer and white acrylic furniture lacquer system
Room niche: two walls at a right angle, floor, possible skirting board
Adult user: reach, door operation, glass handling; child access unknown
Heated indoor dry room: seasonal humidity and temperature cycling, daylight
Postcards and paper items laid between top plate and glass

interfaces.name: Cabinet outer envelope to right-angled room niche

sources: Owner brief 2026-09-04: 'beide Waende 1 m breit', verbal, no measurement record
evidence.uncertainty_note: The only stated figure is a verbal nominal. Real niches deviate by 5-30 mm and 0.5-2 deg. All 13 panel sizes depend on it.

failure_modes.effect: Cabinet cannot be pushed in; back panels bind; front no longer parallel to the niche mouth
failure_modes.mitigation: Measure both wall widths and the corner angle; re-run source with measured values; 15 mm end clearance and 10 mm rear clearance per wall are parameters, not constants

failure_modes.mode: Wall bulge or plaster fillet at the corner
failure_modes.effect: Cabinet stands off the wall, top plate gap grows, cabinet rocks
failure_modes.mitigation: Scribe or increase back_gap; check with a 1 m straightedge

acceptance_criteria: Both wall widths measured at floor, 500 mm and 1000 mm height, recorded to 1 mm
Corner angle measured, deviation from 90 deg recorded
Carcass leg length recomputed as niche_width - back_gap - end_gap and the source re-run

interfaces.name: Adjustable feet to floor: support, levelling and load transfer

sources: Owner brief: feet required so lower doors clear the floor
No floor measurement, no covering identified
evidence.uncertainty_note: Cabinet self mass computed from panel area (about 66 kg in 18 mm birch plywood) plus glass and contents. Floor flatness is UNKNOWN.

interfaces.name: Door to centre partition via 35 mm cup hinge, half-overlay

sources: System 32 nominal geometry: mounting-plate row 37 mm from the front edge, 32 mm hole pitch (furnica.de guide)
Cup 35 mm dia, drilling depth 11.5-12.5 mm, cup centre = 17.5 mm + C (3-6 mm) (furnica.de guide)
Exact hinge article, crank and overlay adjustment range NOT selected

failure_modes.effect: Doors touch each other or leave an oversized centre gap
failure_modes.mitigation: Confirm the article overlay range before drilling; the door gap is a source parameter and can be retuned

Mounting-plate hole row from carcass front edge
Door overlay on the 18 mm partition

interfaces.name: Open-door swing envelope to niche and room keep-out

sources: Swept path computed analytically over the full 0-90 deg opening and verified by geometry check C-18 (four sample points along each leaf, both leaves)
Surrounding room geometry beyond the two 1 m walls is UNKNOWN
evidence.uncertainty_note: Revision 0.1.0 recorded only the PARKED 90 deg position, which stays inside the niche. That was incomplete: a hinged door must swing through the room to reach it. The swept quarter circle has a 539 mm radius about the front midpoint and reaches 1130 mm along each wall direction, i.e. 130 mm beyond each 1 m wall end, and 1377 mm from the corner at its furthest. Whether that space is clear is UNKNOWN.

failure_modes.mode: A return wall or door frame stands at the open end of the niche
failure_modes.effect: Door strikes it before 90 deg; usable opening lost
failure_modes.mitigation: Centre-hinged layout keeps the 90 deg tip inside x,y <= 979 mm; verify the surroundings before building

failure_modes.mode: Handle projects into the swing path of the neighbouring door
failure_modes.effect: Paint damage
failure_modes.mitigation: Handles sit on the outer door edges, hinges at the centre; paths do not cross

failure_modes.mode: Furniture, a door frame or a return wall stands inside the 539 mm swept quarter circle
failure_modes.effect: Door strikes it part-way through the opening even though the parked position is clear
failure_modes.mitigation: C-18 reports the required clear space explicitly. Check it against the real room with a cardboard template before cutting the doors.

acceptance_criteria: Computed door-tip envelope at the 90 deg parked position stays within the measured niche footprint
The full 0-90 deg swept quarter circle, 539 mm radius about the front midpoint, is clear in the real room, checked with a cardboard template before cutting doors
Door leaf does not strike either niche wall at any point of the sweep (geometry check C-18)

interfaces.name: Loose ESG glass plate on the timber top plate with a paper interlayer

sources: ESG 6 mm to size with polished edges is a documented catalogue service; pentagon is a listed special shape on request (glas-ab-werk.de, spiegel21.de)
Glass outline derived from the top-plate polygon by a 2 mm inward offset
Top-plate flatness after painting is UNMEASURED
evidence.uncertainty_note: Wood moisture movement over the seasons is the dominant uncertainty and is not covered by any local measurement.

failure_modes.mode: Top plate cups; rigid glass bears on three points
failure_modes.effect: Glass rocks, cards will not lie flat, local bending stress in the glass
failure_modes.mitigation: Use plywood rather than solid glued softwood for the top plate; seal both faces and all edges; check with a straightedge before ordering the glass

failure_modes.mode: Glass slides on the lacquered surface
failure_modes.effect: Overhang, edge exposure, chipping
failure_modes.mitigation: Optional stainless glass stops at the two wall-side edges, or a 2 mm routed recess

failure_modes.mode: Glass ordered before the built top plate is measured
failure_modes.effect: ESG cannot be recut; the plate is scrap
failure_modes.mitigation: Hard rule: measure the finished top plate, then order the glass

acceptance_criteria: Top plate flat within 1.0 mm over any 900 mm span, measured after painting
Glass gap to the plate edge 1-3 mm all round
Glass does not move under a 20 N horizontal push

No user population defined; child access UNKNOWN

failure_modes.effect: ESG disintegrates into blunt fragments (intended behaviour) but the plate is lost and fragments spread
failure_modes.mitigation: ESG mandatory; 6 mm rather than 4 mm; two-person handling of an 11 kg plate

failure_modes.effect: Bending failure
failure_modes.mitigation: Written handling note in the build manual: lift along an edge, not at a corner

acceptance_criteria: Glass supplied as ESG (tempered) with polished edges and radiused or ground corners, confirmed on the order and the delivery note

interfaces.name: Skirting board and wall build-up to rear panel clearance

sources: Not addressed in the brief. Presence, thickness and height of any skirting board are UNKNOWN.
evidence.uncertainty_note: This is the single cheapest unknown to close and the one most likely to invalidate the cut list.

failure_modes.mode: Skirting thicker than the 10 mm rear clearance
failure_modes.effect: Cabinet stands off the wall by the skirting thickness; the front rotates out of the niche mouth and the top-plate wall gap becomes visible
failure_modes.mitigation: Measure the skirting; set back_gap = skirting thickness + 3 mm, or notch the two back panels, or remove the skirting inside the niche

acceptance_criteria: Skirting thickness and height measured, or absence confirmed
back_gap parameter set from that measurement and the source re-run

drivers: INT (weight 20, score 3): eleven interfaces, hardest at IC 14 (cup-hinge joint and wood-to-climate), including two human-contact interfaces.
PAR (weight 10, score 3): thirteen unique custom panels plus battens, all dimensionally coupled to one datum set.
CPL and PHY (weight 10 each, score 2): every panel size and every hole position derives from the niche datum, and the product carries an 11 kg glass plate plus about 66 kg of panel mass on six feet.

blocking_unknowns: IF-EXT-GEO-CLR-VOLUME-001 at E1: both niche wall widths and the corner angle are verbal nominals with no measurement record.
IF-EXT-GEO-CLR-PLN-011 at E0: skirting board presence, thickness and height are entirely unknown and directly set the rear clearance parameter.
IF-EXT-GEO-SUP-PLN-002 at E1: floor level and covering unknown, foot load rating unselected.
IF-INT-KIN-ROT-CYL-003 at E2: the specific cup-hinge article, its crank and its overlay adjustment range are not selected, so the 7.5 mm half-overlay target is unconfirmed.
IF-EXT-GEO-CON-PLN-008 at E2: whether the store actually used will perform the three 45 deg diagonal cuts is unknown.
IF-ENV-PHY-CON-BODY-009 at E1: no local data on panel flatness stability, which is what the glass plate depends on.

criticality.rationale: An 11 kg tempered glass plate sits at hand height on a free-standing 80 kg cabinet that a child could climb, and the whole unit rests on six adjustable feet loaded through 18 mm panels. None of these is a regulated or expert domain, so K3 is not warranted, but every one of them needs a controlled physical check rather than inspection alone. Failure modes are loss of level, glass movement or breakage, shelf creep and tipping.
credible_failure_effects: Cut to the hand from a glass edge or corner during card exchange (mitigated only by the purchase specification: ESG, polished edges, ground corners).
Glass plate slides off a cupped or unlevelled top plate and breaks.
Cabinet tips or a door fails if a child climbs on an open lower door.
Foot plate tears out of the 18 mm bottom panel under an eccentric point load.
Cut list executed against an unmeasured niche: about 6.2 square metres of panel and a non-recuttable ESG plate become scrap.

decision.rationale: Complexity is C3 and criticality K2, which on their own would place the work in Lane C. Readiness is R1 because the host niche, the single datum from which all thirteen panel sizes and every hole position derive, exists only as a verbal nominal, and the skirting clearance is at E0. Hard gate G2 therefore fails and the lane is forced to E. What this permits is exactly the requested work product: a fully parametric, dimensioned and documented build package plus a concept image, released as CONCEPT_ONLY with a nominal 1000 x 1000 mm niche. It does not permit cutting panels or ordering glass. Revision 0.2.0 changed the footprint on owner request but not the evidence base, so the lane is unchanged. One measurement session closes IF-...-001, -011 and -002, lifts readiness to R3 or better, and moves the project to Lane C with CONDITIONAL confidence.

warnings.message: The host niche is the product's only dimensional datum and is unmeasured. Do not cut any panel against the nominal 1000 x 1000 mm values.
Skirting-board clearance is at E0; floor level and foot load rating at E1. All three set parameters that appear in the cut list.
Lane E. No agent may record a final release, a build approval or a glass order for this revision.
Wall build-up behind the skirting, plaster fillets at the corner and floor covering thickness are not observable from the brief.
Cup hinge, foot, handle and glass supplier articles are specified by function and system dimension only. No article revision is fixed, so the 7.5 mm overlay and the 50 kg foot rating are unconfirmed.
An 11 kg glass plate is handled by hand at every card exchange. ESG, polished edges and ground corners are safety requirements, not finish options, and must appear on the order.
Four hinged doors cycle for the product life and the 18 mm mid shelf is exposed to long-term creep. Both are addressed by purchased-part rating and span limits, neither is tested.

This product has no printed part, nozzle, slicer profile, mesh or calibration coupon. The FDM calibration gate, mesh-simplification gate and slicer dry run are NOT_APPLICABLE and are recorded as such in design-spec.yaml rather than left blank.

The doors sweep a 539 mm radius quarter circle about the front midpoint, reaching 130 mm past each 1 m wall end. Revision 0.1.0 checked only the parked 90 deg position and did not state this. The room-side space is UNMEASURED.

next_actions.action: Measure the niche: both wall widths at floor, 500 mm and 1000 mm height; the corner included angle; wall flatness over 1 m; skirting thickness and height; floor level across the footprint. Record every value with the instrument used.
next_actions.exit_criterion: A measurement record exists in the product folder and IF-EXT-GEO-CLR-VOLUME-001 plus IF-EXT-GEO-CLR-PLN-011 reach E3.

next_actions.action: Re-run source/corner_cabinet.py with the measured niche, back_gap and end_gap, and regenerate the cut list, drill plan and DXF set.
next_actions.exit_criterion: exports/cut-list.csv carries the measured niche in its header and its hash is recorded in the build manifest.

next_actions.action: Select the concrete cup-hinge article and confirm its half-overlay range covers 7.5 mm on an 18 mm partition, plus the foot load rating and the handle hole spacing. Enter each into the component register.
next_actions.exit_criterion: IF-INT-KIN-ROT-CYL-003 reaches E3 and no purchased-part row remains UNKNOWN.

next_actions.action: Mark the 539 mm radius swept quarter circle on the floor in front of the niche with tape or a cardboard door template and confirm nothing stands in it.
next_actions.exit_criterion: IF-EXT-KIN-KOT-VOLUME-004 reaches E3 with the real surroundings recorded.

next_actions.action: Confirm with the chosen store whether it performs the three 45 deg diagonal cuts and its stated tolerance; otherwise plan the guide-rail fallback.
next_actions.exit_criterion: IF-EXT-GEO-CON-PLN-008 reaches E3 with a named store and a stated tolerance.

next_actions.action: Build and paint the carcass, level it in place, then measure the finished top plate and only then order the ESG glass to the as-built outline.
next_actions.exit_criterion: Top plate flat within 1.0 mm over 900 mm and the glass order carries as-built dimensions, ESG, polished edges and ground corners.

next_actions.action: Run the physical acceptance set: door reveal and 90 deg swing, level check, 25 kg shelf load, 200 N open-door tip check.
next_actions.exit_criterion: All acceptance criteria in design-spec.yaml pass and are recorded; readiness reaches R5 for the tested interfaces.
